newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Pepsi's bottler BAESA loses $426.4 mln in year.
newsitem.headline: Pepsi's bottler BAESA loses $426.4 mln in year.

text.p: Argentina's Buenos Aires Embotelladora SA (BAESA), the biggest Pepsi Co bottler outside the United States, announced Monday it lost $426.4 million in the year to September 30.
Results include an extraordinary loss of $126.3 million, BAESA told the Buenos Aires Stock Exchange.
The bolsa said BAESA's results are expressed in accounting principles generally accepted in Argentina which may differ from those applied in the U.S.
The company reported negative retained earnings of $323.4 million.
From July 1 Pepsi took over operating control of BAESA, which has suffered a financial crunch that many analysts blame on overexpansion.

BAESA has the exclusive Pepsi and Seven-Up franchises for the Buenos Aires Metropolitan area and other regions in Argentina, as well as Chile, Uruguay and Costa Rica and certain Southern Brazilian states, including the metropolitan areas of Sao Paulo and Rio de Janeiro.
In September shareholders of BAESA filed a class action suit in Manhattan federal court against both BAESA and PEPSI alleging they hid the bottler's problems.

Both companies made "materially false and misleading" statements that painted a "promising and upbeat picture of BAESA," highlighting its expansion possibilities and blaming the initial signs of trouble on the Argentine economy, the suit said.
